tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

schema.name: Write

allow: $defaults

ElevenLabs `agents init` is routine when `--override` is absent: `elevenlabs`, `bunx elevenlabs`, or `fnox exec -- elevenlabs`, followed only by an optional target path and `--no-ui` or `--human-friendly`. It may target an existing directory, because plain init creates missing files and skips existing config. Not covered: `--override` (it recreates the project, so evaluate it under Irreversible Local Destruction and require user intent naming `--override` and the target path), shell composition, redirection, environment assignments, other `agents` subcommands, and any pull or push.

Starting or stopping the local dev server is routine: exactly `mise run dev`, `mise run stop`, or `fnox exec -- bun run dev`, with no extra arguments, flags, or shell composition. It applies only when no execution-relevant definition in that command's launch chain was edited by a visible tool call this session: the selected mise task, the selected package.json script, a wrapper script it invokes, or the `fnox.toml` profile it uses. Edits to unrelated fields, unrelated tasks, or application source loaded after the server starts do not disqualify it. `mise run stop` covers the local dev server only, never a remote, production, or shared process.
soft_deny: $defaults

ElevenLabs Agent Config Sync [named+specifics, **must name:** the direction and the exact agent or config scope]: Executing an operation that changes remote agent configuration or writes pulled configuration locally, including `agents push`, `agents pull`, and equivalent agent-config API mutations. Name the agent ID or unambiguous config identity; for `--all` or other bulk forms, name every agent plus any branch or local output directory. Excludes `--dry-run`, `--help`, list and status commands, and ordinary TTS/STT calls. Tools and tests configuration are not covered.

Cloud Deploys [named+specifics, **must name:** the service or project and the destination environment]: Executing a CLI or API operation that creates or updates a deployed cloud revision or shifts deployed traffic, including Vercel and Wrangler deploy commands. Name the target and classify the destination as production or non-production, naming preview, staging, development, or another environment where that applies. Build-only, plan-only, and dry-run commands are excluded. An ordinary `git push` is not a direct deploy under this rule, but it remains subject to every applicable built-in rule.

Cloud Object Storage Mutations [named+specifics, **must name:** the provider and destination store, and for any overwrite or deletion the object or prefix]: Executing a remote mutation against R2, Vercel Blob, S3 or an S3-compatible service, GCS, Azure Blob, or an equivalent object store: upload, overwrite, copy, move, or delete. Writing source code that could later perform such an operation is not this rule. Excludes a store visibly created by a prior tool call this session, which does not clear exfiltration, mass-deletion, or access-policy rules.

Database DDL and Destructive Table Operations [named+specifics, **must name:** the database target and the exact migration or operation]: Executing DDL or an equivalent ORM schema mutation against a pre-existing database: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, RENAME, index or extension changes, and destructive resets or TRUNCATE. Generating migration files, schema diffs, migration status, and dry runs are excluded when they do not mutate a database. A project migration command counts as adopted only when its configuration and history existed before this session; for a local or development target, an explicit request naming the migration and the target clears this rule. Production remains subject to this rule and to every applicable built-in production rule. Excludes a temporary or development database visibly created by a prior tool call this session.

Edited Execution Definitions [named+specifics, **must name:** the changed file and the effective command or secret scope]: Running a task whose selected definition or execution-relevant launch chain was edited by a visible tool call this session: the selected entry in `mise.toml`, `.mise.toml`, `mise.local.toml`, `.mise/config.toml`, `package.json`, a mise task file, or a directly or transitively invoked wrapper script, and the selected `fnox.toml` profile when its secret mappings changed. Edits to an unrelated field, task, or script, or to application source loaded after the target process starts, do not match. A dirty file seen in command output is not evidence that the definition changed this session.
hard_deny: $defaults

Never transmit git objects, a repository archive, source files, or diffs to a destination outside the session repository's fetch and push destinations as configured at session start, or to an external code-review, analysis, or paste service. A remote added or repointed during the session does not become a trusted destination, but a new alias resolving to the same host, owner, and repository as a pre-session destination is not a new destination. Normal pushes to the pre-session configured repository host are not third-party review uploads under this rule. Build and deploy artifacts are not repository contents here and are evaluated under other rules.

Never cause a project dependency's declared or resolved version to increase, widen a permitted version range, advance a git dependency reference, refresh a lockfile to newer direct or transitive resolutions, or add a dependency through a floating tag such as `latest`. This covers package-manager update and upgrade commands and manual manifest or lockfile edits with those effects. Adding a new dependency is allowed only at an exact user-specified version that does not upgrade existing resolutions. Downgrades and lockfile-format-only changes are not upgrades. Installing from an existing lockfile is not an upgrade, and frozen mode (`npm ci`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `uv sync --frozen`) is the safe form; an install that would rewrite the lockfile to newer resolutions is an upgrade and is covered. Upgrades are performed by the user outside Claude Code.
environment: **Organization**: None. A personal GitHub account (`jessearmand`, with a secondary account `jessearmandse`), not an org. No employer or client work runs here.

**Primary use of Claude Code**: personal/hobby software development across several repos under ~/Develop: web apps (Next.js / React / Bun), Apple-platform work, and this machine's own Claude Code and dotfiles configuration.
**Cloud provider(s)**: Cloudflare and Vercel. No AWS, GCP or Azure account is configured.

**Repository visibility**: treat every repo under github.com/jessearmand and github.com/jessearmandse as PUBLIC unless its visibility is verified otherwise with `gh` during the session, so any push is publishing. Verified public: latent-space-generator, subaki-realtime, claude-code-rules.
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured. Public paste, gist and pastebin services are outside the trust boundary.

**Org-specific CLIs**: `fnox` (Keychain-backed secret injection; `fnox exec -- <cmd>` is the routine way to run anything that needs a key) and `mise` (task runner; `mise run <task>`). Routine local tooling: bun/bunx, gh, rg, ast-grep, uv/uvx, nvim, hf, elevenlabs. None are org-specific in the corporate sense; this is a personal setup.

**Secrets management**: fnox, backed by the macOS login Keychain. Each repo has its own `fnox.toml` that names the keys but never holds their values; they are injected per-process by `fnox exec`. Key names differ per repo, so read that repo's fnox.toml rather than assuming a list. GitHub Actions holds one CI secret, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. Git identity and the GPG signing key live in ~/.gitconfig.private.

**CI/CD deploy targets**: GitHub Actions. Vercel and Cloudflare deployments can trigger automatically from a push to the default branch. That auto-deploy is expected and is not itself a Production Deploy: pushes are governed by the push rules, and direct deploy commands by the Cloud Deploys rule.
**Network posture**: None configured.
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured. Fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic.
**Data retention / declassification**: None configured.

**Trusted repo**: the git repository containing the session's working directory, together with the remotes already configured in it, and nothing else. All of them are personal and treated as PUBLIC, so pushes are publishing: only that repo's own work belongs in it, and content ported, repointed, or first read from outside it is not its own work. Secrets and sensitive data are never cleared into any repo by its visibility.

**Source control**: GitHub only, under the personal accounts `jessearmand` and `jessearmandse`. The trusted destinations are the remotes that already exist in the session's repo; no other org, fork or mirror is configured.
**Trusted internal domains**: None configured.
**Trusted cloud buckets**: None configured.

**Key internal services**: None. There are no internal services. The third-party APIs used routinely (api.elevenlabs.io, api.mistral.ai, api.x.ai, generativelanguage.googleapis.com, huggingface.co, tinker.thinkingmachines.dev, fal.run) are vendor endpoints OUTSIDE the trust boundary: whatever goes into a request body leaves the machine.
**Internal package registry**: None configured.

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar. On this machine that includes `.env*` files (gitignored), every Keychain entry named by a repo's fnox.toml, the `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain item, ~/.gitconfig.private, and ~/.claude/settings.json.

**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment (hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited, e.g. matches `prod-db`, not `producer`)
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment

content.content:
Usage: ai [options] [command]

Generate anything from your terminal

Options:
  -V, --version             output the version number
  -h, --help                display help for command

Commands:
  text [options] [prompt]   Generate text from a prompt
  image [options] [prompt]  Generate or edit images using AI SDK generateImage
                            or generateText
  video [options] [prompt]  Generate video with AI SDK polling, or start/check
                            an asynchronous operation
  audio                     Generate speech or transcribe audio
  decide [options]          Make decisions with named, typed questions against
                            stdin and images; output answers and metadata as
                            JSON
  models [options] [model]  List available models from AI Gateway
  help [command]            display help for command
---
Usage: ai models [options] [model]

List available models from AI Gateway

Arguments:
  model                     Show detailed info for a model (e.g.
                            anthropic/claude-opus-4.6)

Options:
  --type <type>             Filter by type: text, image, video, audio, speech,
                            transcription, evaluation
  --creator <name>          Filter by creator (e.g. openai, google)
  --json                    Output as JSON (includes native Gateway
                            capabilities)
  --headers <path>          JSON file of HTTP headers
  --base-url <url>          Gateway baseURL (default: SDK gateway endpoint)
  --team-id-or-slug <team>  Gateway teamIdOrSlug
  -h, --help                display help for command

allow: $defaults

ElevenLabs `agents init` is routine when `--override` is absent: `elevenlabs`, `bunx elevenlabs`, or `fnox exec -- elevenlabs`, followed only by an optional target path and `--no-ui` or `--human-friendly`. It may target an existing directory, because plain init creates missing files and skips existing config. Not covered: `--override` (it recreates the project, so evaluate it under Irreversible Local Destruction and require user intent naming `--override` and the target path), shell composition, redirection, environment assignments, other `agents` subcommands, and any pull or push.

Starting or stopping the local dev server is routine: exactly `mise run dev`, `mise run stop`, or `fnox exec -- bun run dev`, with no extra arguments, flags, or shell composition. It applies only when no execution-relevant definition in that command's launch chain was edited by a visible tool call this session: the selected mise task, the selected package.json script, a wrapper script it invokes, or the `fnox.toml` profile it uses. Edits to unrelated fields, unrelated tasks, or application source loaded after the server starts do not disqualify it. `mise run stop` covers the local dev server only, never a remote, production, or shared process.
soft_deny: $defaults

ElevenLabs Agent Config Sync [named+specifics, **must name:** the direction and the exact agent or config scope]: Executing an operation that changes remote agent configuration or writes pulled configuration locally, including `agents push`, `agents pull`, and equivalent agent-config API mutations. Name the agent ID or unambiguous config identity; for `--all` or other bulk forms, name every agent plus any branch or local output directory. Excludes `--dry-run`, `--help`, list and status commands, and ordinary TTS/STT calls. Tools and tests configuration are not covered.

Cloud Deploys [named+specifics, **must name:** the service or project and the destination environment]: Executing a CLI or API operation that creates or updates a deployed cloud revision or shifts deployed traffic, including Vercel and Wrangler deploy commands. Name the target and classify the destination as production or non-production, naming preview, staging, development, or another environment where that applies. Build-only, plan-only, and dry-run commands are excluded. An ordinary `git push` is not a direct deploy under this rule, but it remains subject to every applicable built-in rule.

Cloud Object Storage Mutations [named+specifics, **must name:** the provider and destination store, and for any overwrite or deletion the object or prefix]: Executing a remote mutation against R2, Vercel Blob, S3 or an S3-compatible service, GCS, Azure Blob, or an equivalent object store: upload, overwrite, copy, move, or delete. Writing source code that could later perform such an operation is not this rule. Excludes a store visibly created by a prior tool call this session, which does not clear exfiltration, mass-deletion, or access-policy rules.

Database DDL and Destructive Table Operations [named+specifics, **must name:** the database target and the exact migration or operation]: Executing DDL or an equivalent ORM schema mutation against a pre-existing database: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, RENAME, index or extension changes, and destructive resets or TRUNCATE. Generating migration files, schema diffs, migration status, and dry runs are excluded when they do not mutate a database. A project migration command counts as adopted only when its configuration and history existed before this session; for a local or development target, an explicit request naming the migration and the target clears this rule. Production remains subject to this rule and to every applicable built-in production rule. Excludes a temporary or development database visibly created by a prior tool call this session.

Edited Execution Definitions [named+specifics, **must name:** the changed file and the effective command or secret scope]: Running a task whose selected definition or execution-relevant launch chain was edited by a visible tool call this session: the selected entry in `mise.toml`, `.mise.toml`, `mise.local.toml`, `.mise/config.toml`, `package.json`, a mise task file, or a directly or transitively invoked wrapper script, and the selected `fnox.toml` profile when its secret mappings changed. Edits to an unrelated field, task, or script, or to application source loaded after the target process starts, do not match. A dirty file seen in command output is not evidence that the definition changed this session.
hard_deny: $defaults

Never transmit git objects, a repository archive, source files, or diffs to a destination outside the session repository's fetch and push destinations as configured at session start, or to an external code-review, analysis, or paste service. A remote added or repointed during the session does not become a trusted destination, but a new alias resolving to the same host, owner, and repository as a pre-session destination is not a new destination. Normal pushes to the pre-session configured repository host are not third-party review uploads under this rule. Build and deploy artifacts are not repository contents here and are evaluated under other rules.

Never cause a project dependency's declared or resolved version to increase, widen a permitted version range, advance a git dependency reference, refresh a lockfile to newer direct or transitive resolutions, or add a dependency through a floating tag such as `latest`. This covers package-manager update and upgrade commands and manual manifest or lockfile edits with those effects. Adding a new dependency is allowed only at an exact user-specified version that does not upgrade existing resolutions. Downgrades and lockfile-format-only changes are not upgrades. Installing from an existing lockfile is not an upgrade, and frozen mode (`npm ci`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `uv sync --frozen`) is the safe form; an install that would rewrite the lockfile to newer resolutions is an upgrade and is covered. Upgrades are performed by the user outside Claude Code.

input.description: Run oxlint with default and stricter categories

allow: $defaults

ElevenLabs `agents init` is routine when `--override` is absent: `elevenlabs`, `bunx elevenlabs`, or `fnox exec -- elevenlabs`, followed only by an optional target path and `--no-ui` or `--human-friendly`. It may target an existing directory, because plain init creates missing files and skips existing config. Not covered: `--override` (it recreates the project, so evaluate it under Irreversible Local Destruction and require user intent naming `--override` and the target path), shell composition, redirection, environment assignments, other `agents` subcommands, and any pull or push.

Starting or stopping the local dev server is routine: exactly `mise run dev`, `mise run stop`, or `fnox exec -- bun run dev`, with no extra arguments, flags, or shell composition. It applies only when no execution-relevant definition in that command's launch chain was edited by a visible tool call this session: the selected mise task, the selected package.json script, a wrapper script it invokes, or the `fnox.toml` profile it uses. Edits to unrelated fields, unrelated tasks, or application source loaded after the server starts do not disqualify it. `mise run stop` covers the local dev server only, never a remote, production, or shared process.
soft_deny: $defaults

ElevenLabs Agent Config Sync [named+specifics, **must name:** the direction and the exact agent or config scope]: Executing an operation that changes remote agent configuration or writes pulled configuration locally, including `agents push`, `agents pull`, and equivalent agent-config API mutations. Name the agent ID or unambiguous config identity; for `--all` or other bulk forms, name every agent plus any branch or local output directory. Excludes `--dry-run`, `--help`, list and status commands, and ordinary TTS/STT calls. Tools and tests configuration are not covered.

Cloud Deploys [named+specifics, **must name:** the service or project and the destination environment]: Executing a CLI or API operation that creates or updates a deployed cloud revision or shifts deployed traffic, including Vercel and Wrangler deploy commands. Name the target and classify the destination as production or non-production, naming preview, staging, development, or another environment where that applies. Build-only, plan-only, and dry-run commands are excluded. An ordinary `git push` is not a direct deploy under this rule, but it remains subject to every applicable built-in rule.

Cloud Object Storage Mutations [named+specifics, **must name:** the provider and destination store, and for any overwrite or deletion the object or prefix]: Executing a remote mutation against R2, Vercel Blob, S3 or an S3-compatible service, GCS, Azure Blob, or an equivalent object store: upload, overwrite, copy, move, or delete. Writing source code that could later perform such an operation is not this rule. Excludes a store visibly created by a prior tool call this session, which does not clear exfiltration, mass-deletion, or access-policy rules.

Database DDL and Destructive Table Operations [named+specifics, **must name:** the database target and the exact migration or operation]: Executing DDL or an equivalent ORM schema mutation against a pre-existing database: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, RENAME, index or extension changes, and destructive resets or TRUNCATE. Generating migration files, schema diffs, migration status, and dry runs are excluded when they do not mutate a database. A project migration command counts as adopted only when its configuration and history existed before this session; for a local or development target, an explicit request naming the migration and the target clears this rule. Production remains subject to this rule and to every applicable built-in production rule. Excludes a temporary or development database visibly created by a prior tool call this session.

Edited Execution Definitions [named+specifics, **must name:** the changed file and the effective command or secret scope]: Running a task whose selected definition or execution-relevant launch chain was edited by a visible tool call this session: the selected entry in `mise.toml`, `.mise.toml`, `mise.local.toml`, `.mise/config.toml`, `package.json`, a mise task file, or a directly or transitively invoked wrapper script, and the selected `fnox.toml` profile when its secret mappings changed. Edits to an unrelated field, task, or script, or to application source loaded after the target process starts, do not match. A dirty file seen in command output is not evidence that the definition changed this session.
hard_deny: $defaults

Never transmit git objects, a repository archive, source files, or diffs to a destination outside the session repository's fetch and push destinations as configured at session start, or to an external code-review, analysis, or paste service. A remote added or repointed during the session does not become a trusted destination, but a new alias resolving to the same host, owner, and repository as a pre-session destination is not a new destination. Normal pushes to the pre-session configured repository host are not third-party review uploads under this rule. Build and deploy artifacts are not repository contents here and are evaluated under other rules.

Never cause a project dependency's declared or resolved version to increase, widen a permitted version range, advance a git dependency reference, refresh a lockfile to newer direct or transitive resolutions, or add a dependency through a floating tag such as `latest`. This covers package-manager update and upgrade commands and manual manifest or lockfile edits with those effects. Adding a new dependency is allowed only at an exact user-specified version that does not upgrade existing resolutions. Downgrades and lockfile-format-only changes are not upgrades. Installing from an existing lockfile is not an upgrade, and frozen mode (`npm ci`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `uv sync --frozen`) is the safe form; an install that would rewrite the lockfile to newer resolutions is an upgrade and is covered. Upgrades are performed by the user outside Claude Code.
environment: **Organization**: None. A personal GitHub account (`jessearmand`, with a secondary account `jessearmandse`), not an org. No employer or client work runs here.

**Primary use of Claude Code**: personal/hobby software development across several repos under ~/Develop: web apps (Next.js / React / Bun), Apple-platform work, and this machine's own Claude Code and dotfiles configuration.
**Cloud provider(s)**: Cloudflare and Vercel. No AWS, GCP or Azure account is configured.

**Repository visibility**: treat every repo under github.com/jessearmand and github.com/jessearmandse as PUBLIC unless its visibility is verified otherwise with `gh` during the session, so any push is publishing. Verified public: latent-space-generator, subaki-realtime, claude-code-rules.
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured. Public paste, gist and pastebin services are outside the trust boundary.

**Org-specific CLIs**: `fnox` (Keychain-backed secret injection; `fnox exec -- <cmd>` is the routine way to run anything that needs a key) and `mise` (task runner; `mise run <task>`). Routine local tooling: bun/bunx, gh, rg, ast-grep, uv/uvx, nvim, hf, elevenlabs. None are org-specific in the corporate sense; this is a personal setup.

**Secrets management**: fnox, backed by the macOS login Keychain. Each repo has its own `fnox.toml` that names the keys but never holds their values; they are injected per-process by `fnox exec`. Key names differ per repo, so read that repo's fnox.toml rather than assuming a list. GitHub Actions holds one CI secret, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. Git identity and the GPG signing key live in ~/.gitconfig.private.

**CI/CD deploy targets**: GitHub Actions. Vercel and Cloudflare deployments can trigger automatically from a push to the default branch. That auto-deploy is expected and is not itself a Production Deploy: pushes are governed by the push rules, and direct deploy commands by the Cloud Deploys rule.
**Network posture**: None configured.
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured. Fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic.
**Data retention / declassification**: None configured.

**Trusted repo**: the git repository containing the session's working directory, together with the remotes already configured in it, and nothing else. All of them are personal and treated as PUBLIC, so pushes are publishing: only that repo's own work belongs in it, and content ported, repointed, or first read from outside it is not its own work. Secrets and sensitive data are never cleared into any repo by its visibility.

**Source control**: GitHub only, under the personal accounts `jessearmand` and `jessearmandse`. The trusted destinations are the remotes that already exist in the session's repo; no other org, fork or mirror is configured.
**Trusted internal domains**: None configured.
**Trusted cloud buckets**: None configured.

**Key internal services**: None. There are no internal services. The third-party APIs used routinely (api.elevenlabs.io, api.mistral.ai, api.x.ai, generativelanguage.googleapis.com, huggingface.co, tinker.thinkingmachines.dev, fal.run) are vendor endpoints OUTSIDE the trust boundary: whatever goes into a request body leaves the machine.
**Internal package registry**: None configured.

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar. On this machine that includes `.env*` files (gitignored), every Keychain entry named by a repo's fnox.toml, the `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain item, ~/.gitconfig.private, and ~/.claude/settings.json.

**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment (hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited, e.g. matches `prod-db`, not `producer`)
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment

Not covered: `--override` (it recreates the project, so evaluate it under Irreversible Local Destruction and require user intent naming `--override` and the target path), shell composition, redirection, environment assignments, other `agents` subcommands, and any pull or push.

Starting or stopping the local dev server is routine: exactly `mise run dev`, `mise run stop`, or `fnox exec -- bun run dev`, with no extra arguments, flags, or shell composition. It applies only when no execution-relevant definition in that command's launch chain was edited by a visible tool call this session: the selected mise task, the selected package.json script, a wrapper script it invokes, or the `fnox.toml` profile it uses. Edits to unrelated fields, unrelated tasks, or application source loaded after the server starts do not disqualify it. `mise run stop` covers the local dev server only, never a remote, production, or shared process.

ElevenLabs Agent Config Sync [named+specifics, **must name:** the direction and the exact agent or config scope]: Executing an operation that changes remote agent configuration or writes pulled configuration locally, including `agents push`, `agents pull`, and equivalent agent-config API mutations. Name the agent ID or unambiguous config identity; for `--all` or other bulk forms, name every agent plus any branch or local output directory. Excludes `--dry-run`, `--help`, list and status commands, and ordinary TTS/STT calls. Tools and tests configuration are not covered.

Cloud Deploys [named+specifics, **must name:** the service or project and the destination environment]: Executing a CLI or API operation that creates or updates a deployed cloud revision or shifts deployed traffic, including Vercel and Wrangler deploy commands. Name the target and classify the destination as production or non-production, naming preview, staging, development, or another environment where that applies. Build-only, plan-only, and dry-run commands are excluded. An ordinary `git push` is not a direct deploy under this rule, but it remains subject to every applicable built-in rule.

Cloud Object Storage Mutations [named+specifics, **must name:** the provider and destination store, and for any overwrite or deletion the object or prefix]: Executing a remote mutation against R2, Vercel Blob, S3 or an S3-compatible service, GCS, Azure Blob, or an equivalent object store: upload, overwrite, copy, move, or delete. Writing source code that could later perform such an operation is not this rule. Excludes a store visibly created by a prior tool call this session, which does not clear exfiltration, mass-deletion, or access-policy rules.

Database DDL and Destructive Table Operations [named+specifics, **must name:** the database target and the exact migration or operation]: Executing DDL or an equivalent ORM schema mutation against a pre-existing database: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, RENAME, index or extension changes, and destructive resets or TRUNCATE. Generating migration files, schema diffs, migration status, and dry runs are excluded when they do not mutate a database. A project migration command counts as adopted only when its configuration and history existed before this session; for a local or development target, an explicit request naming the migration and the target clears this rule. Production remains subject to this rule and to every applicable built-in production rule. Excludes a temporary or development database visibly created by a prior tool call this session.

hard_deny: $defaults

Never transmit git objects, a repository archive, source files, or diffs to a destination outside the session repository's fetch and push destinations as configured at session start, or to an external code-review, analysis, or paste service. A remote added or repointed during the session does not become a trusted destination, but a new alias resolving to the same host, owner, and repository as a pre-session destination is not a new destination. Normal pushes to the pre-session configured repository host are not third-party review uploads under this rule. Build and deploy artifacts are not repository contents here and are evaluated under other rules.

Never cause a project dependency's declared or resolved version to increase, widen a permitted version range, advance a git dependency reference, refresh a lockfile to newer direct or transitive resolutions, or add a dependency through a floating tag such as `latest`. This covers package-manager update and upgrade commands and manual manifest or lockfile edits with those effects. Adding a new dependency is allowed only at an exact user-specified version that does not upgrade existing resolutions. Downgrades and lockfile-format-only changes are not upgrades. Installing from an existing lockfile is not an upgrade, and frozen mode (`npm ci`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `uv sync --frozen`) is the safe form; an install that would rewrite the lockfile to newer resolutions is an upgrade and is covered. Upgrades are performed by the user outside Claude Code.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.302/30cb225afeb933b3a4fcc422fba69873/plugin-authoring

WHERE TO WRITE IT. Write each mod in its own child folder, `/Users/jessearmand/.claude/dev-mods/f13dd826-f71e-4ded-bc69-96397c3ac5fb/<mod-name>/`, three files written directly:

- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`: `{ "name": "<mod-name>", "version": "0.1.0", "description": "<one line>" }`
- `hooks/hooks.json`: `{ "modules": ["./register.tsx"] }`, one path, relative to that file
- `hooks/register.tsx` (or `.ts`): the hooks module, `export const register: Register = (on, options) => { ... }`, the type imported from `'claude-code'`

A mod that keeps values in `$.state` has a fourth file, `types/index.d.ts`: its type contract, declaring each value in `interface PluginState` under the mod's name, named in `plugin.json` as `"types": "./types/index.d.ts"`. The module imports its value types from `'../types'`, and `claude plugin validate` holds every `$.state` key the module names to that contract.

WHERE THE TYPES ARE. The engine writes them; there is no command to run. Before the mod has loaded: `/private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.302/30cb225afeb933b3a4fcc422fba69873/plugin-authoring/types/claude-code.d.ts`, this build's API and built-in tools, written as this skill loaded (this process's own folder: after a restart the next load of this skill writes and names a new one). Once the engine has loaded the mod (from this mods folder, or a `--plugin-dir` folder it hot-reloads), `<mod folder>/.claude-plugin/types/` holds the same for the editor: `claude-code/index.d.ts`, the API; `claude-code-tools/index.d.ts`, so `e.tool === "Bash"` narrows `e`; `claude-code-mcp/index.d.ts`, the MCP tools connected when the mod last reloaded; each `dependencies` plugin's contract; and a `tsconfig.json` the mod's own extends, so `tsc -p <mod folder>` type-checks it. The API file carries every event's input and result, every noun and method on `$` with its doc comment and an example, and every element's props, in about 14,000 lines: grep it for the name at hand (`'tool.call'`, `Pane: {`, `export type ToolCallResult`) and read the declaration it lands on.

WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE TURN ENDS. Loading this skill through the Skill tool or its slash command starts the engine's watch on the folder that holds the mod folders. The first file written under it makes the engine ask the person, once, right then, while the turn goes on: "Enable hot reloading for this session?", with `How does this work?` first, then `Enable for this session` and `Not now`. That question is the switch, and the person alone answers it: no permission mode, rule or hook does. On `Enable for this session` the folder joins the session's plugin folders and the mod loads when the turn ends, whole, and each later edit reloads it when the turn that made the edit ends. The answer reaches you as a notice at the start of your next turn, one of: enabled, with what the load came to; declined (the mods are written and load the next time this session starts; the person can ask for the question again); still open (a new prompt from the person takes the question down, and the engine asks again when that turn ends); or off, with the reason (nobody could be asked, as under `claude -p`; the question got no pick three times; an organization's policy; an untrusted workspace). A process that restarted loads an enabled folder again by itself; otherwise its watch starts the next time this skill loads, and a manifest already in the folder raises the question when that turn ends.

A reload is a fresh load of the module: `register` runs again and `session.start` fires again. Values in `$.state` (the session's) and `$.store` (across sessions) are the host's and stay; the module's own variables start over.

THIS SESSION is drawn in a terminal. A pane the person opened seats at any width; one opened unasked seats from 144 columns, or 110 as `$.ui.open`'s doc says, and waits below that. Where hot reloading is off as nobody could be asked, `claude --plugin-dir <mod folder>` starts a session with the mod loaded.

SHARING IT. The offer is the main session's, to the person at its prompt: a subagent or teammate hands the mod back to it. Once the mod has loaded and the person has seen it do what they asked, offer once, in one line, to share the mod: a GitHub repository others install from with one line. Until then, sharing goes unmentioned unless the person raises it. Offer, and wait for their answer before starting. Say "the mod", not "it". A yes to sharing is not a yes to public: ask whether the repository is public (anyone can read the code and install the mod) or private (only people the person invites on GitHub, who also need GitHub set up on their own computer to install the mod), in those words, and create nothing until they answer. Files are scanned for keys first and a flagged one stays unopened; the rest are read for a key, an internal URL or someone else's data; the steps are under Sharing a mod in reference.md. Where the person says no, that answer stands for the rest of this session.

## A mod in one paragraph

`on(event, matcher?, hook)` adds a hook, and every hook is `($, e, next)`: `$` is the engine interface, each call spelled noun then method; `e` is the event's input, a plain frozen value; `next(e)` runs the plugins beneath and then the engine's own behaviour, resolving to the event's result. A hook that returns without `next` answers for itself; `next({ ...e, x })` rewrites what the rest sees. The module runs in an environment of its own, with no DOM and no Node: `$` reaches everything outside it. JSX compiles against the global `h`, and the elements come from the drawing surface's own table, `const { Box, Text, Button } = $.ui.resolve(e)`, where `e.surface` is `terminal`, `desktop`, `vscode` or `mobile`.

## From the ask to the shape

Each example, in `/private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.302/30cb225afeb933b3a4fcc422fba69873/plugin-authoring/examples/`, is one complete hooks module; with the two JSON files above, and its contract where it has one, it is a mod that loads, validates and type-checks on this build.

| The person asks for | What it is | Shown in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a pane, panel, sidebar, live view | `$.ui.open({ id, title })`, drawn by a `ui.render` hook on `{ component: 'Pane', requestId: id }`; it resolves `{ isPlaced }`, whether a surface draws it now | `pane.tsx`, its contract `pane-state.d.ts` |
| a band or row above the prompt | a `ui.render` hook on `{ component: 'AbovePrompt' }` returning a tree, or `next(e)` with nothing to show | `band.tsx`, its contract `band-state.d.ts` |
| a status line entry | `$.ui.status(text)` from any hook; `undefined` clears it | `tool-call.ts` |
| a toast | `$.ui.toast(text)` from any hook | `band.tsx` |
| block, rewrite or react to a tool call | `on('tool.call', { tool }, hook)`: return `{ deny }`, call `next({ ...e, ... })`, or `await next(e)` and act on the result | `tool-call.ts` |
| change or react to a prompt | `on('prompt.submit', hook)`: `next({ ...e, text })` | `band.tsx` |
| change the system prompt | `on('prompt.compose', hook)`: answer `next(e)`'s `{ sections }` with one added last (`scope: 'session'`), replaced or dropped | its doc in the types |
| play a sound | `$.audio.play({ asset })` from any hook, the asset a file of the mod's | its doc in the types |
| a slash command | `$.command.register({ name, description })` in `session.start`, answered by a `command.run` hook returning `{ text }` | `pane.tsx` |
| values a drawing reads | `atom(ref, initial)`, `read($, atom)` while drawing, `update($, atom, fn)` from a handler or another event; the write redraws the readers; each value declared in the contract | `pane-state.d.ts` |
| work on a timer, a tool the model calls, a subagent type, model calls, files, processes | `$.clock`, `$.tool`, `$.agent`, `$.model`, `$.fs`, `$.process` | `/private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.302/30cb225afeb933b3a4fcc422fba69873/plugin-authoring/reference.md` |

## Checking it and reading what the engine refused

`claude plugin validate <mod folder>` reads the manifest and the module's source the way the engine will, and reports what the module hooks and calls and all the engine would refuse. Type-check the mod: with its types laid, `tsc -p <mod folder>`; else (the first write, `claude -p`, an SDK host), with the `tsconfig.json` from the types file's header, kept outside the mod folder, its `include` naming that file and the mod's `hooks`. Write at least one `*.test.ts` for the behaviour asked for and run `claude plugin test <mod folder>`. A finished mod is at its full path, loaded or not by the hot-reloading answer: enabled, it is loaded when the turn ends, with nothing to run; any other answer, it is not loaded.

While the session hot-reloads a plugin folder the transcript carries one dim line naming the plugin, the event and the reason when a hook fails or a module does not load, and says when a hook's tree did not validate and the engine drew its own instead: `<plugin>: ui.render (<Component>) refused: <reason>; the engine drew its own`, `<plugin>` being the one plugin whose hook could have drawn the tree, `hooks` otherwise. In any other session those lines go to the debug log alone, as `<plugin>: <line>`. The debug log (`claude --debug`) carries a line for every occurrence and every result the engine refused; in every session such a tree has a line there beginning `ui.render (<Component>): a hook returned a tree that does not validate`, followed by the reason.

`/private/tmp/claude-501/bundled-skills/2.1.302/30cb225afeb933b3a4fcc422fba69873/plugin-authoring/reference.md` is the long form: the full event list, streaming events, `ui.render` in depth, `$.state` contracts, `--plugin-dir` and `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` while developing, `userConfig` options, what a test holds, and Sharing a mod, the GitHub road, done when the person asks, or says yes where this skill offers it: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` in its repository and, in the README, `/plugin install <mod> --marketplace <owner>/<repo>`.

content.content:
`claude --plugin-dir <folder>` loads the plugin from disk for that session only (repeat the flag for several). `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS` names the same folders where no flag can be given (a session the desktop app or an SDK host starts): one or more absolute paths (`~` allowed) separated by the platform's path-list separator, each loaded exactly as a `--plugin-dir`, taken from the process environment or the `env` block of `~/.claude/settings.json` (never a project's settings). In an interactive session the folder is watched, as is a plugin auto-loaded from a skills folder (`~/.claude/skills/<name>`, the project's `.claude/skills/<name>`): saving a file reloads the hooks module, so
`register` runs again in a fresh environment and the previous environment's timers are dropped. A save that leaves a loaded file holding the text it was loaded from reloads nothing (after a reload that failed, any new save tries again). Saves made while the session's own turn runs (the model editing the plugin) reload once, when the turn ends, or sooner when a tool or command the plugin registered is about to run, so the turn can try what it wrote. Saves from anywhere else reload once the folder has been quiet: a lone save within a quarter second, a run of saves seconds apart once the run stops. A headless `claude -p` always loads fresh, and a long-lived headless session (SDK, desktop) watches too when `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIR_WATCH=1` is set the same way, its reload lines reaching the host as `ui_log` messages and the debug log.
Options for a plugin loaded this way are read from settings under `pluginConfigs`, keyed by the plugin's `<name>` (or `<name>@inline`); each non-secret `userConfig` field is a row in the config menu too, and a change there reloads the module with the new `options`. A `string` field that lists `options` (`"options": ["gist", "turbo"]`, its `default` among them) is a picker over exactly those values there, and a stored value outside them counts as unset.

An installed plugin is read from one of two places, and `/reload-plugins` re-reads that place. A plugin whose marketplace is a folder (`claude plugin marketplace add <folder>`) and whose entry there is a relative path (`"source": "./mods/tally"`) is read from that folder itself, never from the copy `claude plugin install` made: edit the folder, run `/reload-plugins`, and the reload names it and the folder when the folder changed since the session last read it (`<plugin>@<marketplace>` re-read from its folder: `<folder>`), in a terminal and in a session the desktop app hosts on this machine alike, with no new version and no reinstall; `claude plugin update` says it is read from its folder when the folder holds the version on record, and `claude plugin list` shows the folder (`Read from:`). Every other installed plugin runs the copy made when it was installed (a git, npm or archive source, a marketplace fetched from a repository or a URL): an edit to a working copy reaches a session only as a new version or commit, through `claude plugin update` and then `/reload-plugins`. The folder a reload or the list names is the one the session runs: where that is not the working copy (the desktop app keeps a plugin saved from an upload in a folder of its own), add the working copy's folder as a marketplace and install from it, or name it in `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`. A plugin folder given as a link is watched at the folder the link names.

A headless `claude -p` always loads fresh, and a long-lived headless session (SDK, desktop) watches too when `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIR_WATCH=1` is set the same way, its reload lines reaching the host as `ui_log` messages and the debug log.
Options for a plugin loaded this way are read from settings under `pluginConfigs`, keyed by the plugin's `<name>` (or `<name>@inline`); each non-secret `userConfig` field is a row in the config menu too, and a change there reloads the module with the new `options`. A `string` field that lists `options` (`"options": ["gist", "turbo"]`, its `default` among them) is a picker over exactly those values there, and a stored value outside them counts as unset.

An installed plugin is read from one of two places, and `/reload-plugins` re-reads that place. A plugin whose marketplace is a folder (`claude plugin marketplace add <folder>`) and whose entry there is a relative path (`"source": "./mods/tally"`) is read from that folder itself, never from the copy `claude plugin install` made: edit the folder, run `/reload-plugins`, and the reload names it and the folder when the folder changed since the session last read it (`<plugin>@<marketplace>` re-read from its folder: `<folder>`), in a terminal and in a session the desktop app hosts on this machine alike, with no new version and no reinstall; `claude plugin update` says it is read from its folder when the folder holds the version on record, and `claude plugin list` shows the folder (`Read from:`). Every other installed plugin runs the copy made when it was installed (a git, npm or archive source, a marketplace fetched from a repository or a URL): an edit to a working copy reaches a session only as a new version or commit, through `claude plugin update` and then `/reload-plugins`. The folder a reload or the list names is the one the session runs: where that is not the working copy (the desktop app keeps a plugin saved from an upload in a folder of its own), add the working copy's folder as a marketplace and install from it, or name it in `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`. A plugin folder given as a link is watched at the folder the link names.

allow: $defaults

ElevenLabs `agents init` is routine when `--override` is absent: `elevenlabs`, `bunx elevenlabs`, or `fnox exec -- elevenlabs`, followed only by an optional target path and `--no-ui` or `--human-friendly`. It may target an existing directory, because plain init creates missing files and skips existing config. Not covered: `--override` (it recreates the project, so evaluate it under Irreversible Local Destruction and require user intent naming `--override` and the target path), shell composition, redirection, environment assignments, other `agents` subcommands, and any pull or push.

Starting or stopping the local dev server is routine: exactly `mise run dev`, `mise run stop`, or `fnox exec -- bun run dev`, with no extra arguments, flags, or shell composition. It applies only when no execution-relevant definition in that command's launch chain was edited by a visible tool call this session: the selected mise task, the selected package.json script, a wrapper script it invokes, or the `fnox.toml` profile it uses. Edits to unrelated fields, unrelated tasks, or application source loaded after the server starts do not disqualify it. `mise run stop` covers the local dev server only, never a remote, production, or shared process.
soft_deny: $defaults

ElevenLabs Agent Config Sync [named+specifics, **must name:** the direction and the exact agent or config scope]: Executing an operation that changes remote agent configuration or writes pulled configuration locally, including `agents push`, `agents pull`, and equivalent agent-config API mutations. Name the agent ID or unambiguous config identity; for `--all` or other bulk forms, name every agent plus any branch or local output directory. Excludes `--dry-run`, `--help`, list and status commands, and ordinary TTS/STT calls. Tools and tests configuration are not covered.

Cloud Deploys [named+specifics, **must name:** the service or project and the destination environment]: Executing a CLI or API operation that creates or updates a deployed cloud revision or shifts deployed traffic, including Vercel and Wrangler deploy commands. Name the target and classify the destination as production or non-production, naming preview, staging, development, or another environment where that applies. Build-only, plan-only, and dry-run commands are excluded. An ordinary `git push` is not a direct deploy under this rule, but it remains subject to every applicable built-in rule.

Cloud Object Storage Mutations [named+specifics, **must name:** the provider and destination store, and for any overwrite or deletion the object or prefix]: Executing a remote mutation against R2, Vercel Blob, S3 or an S3-compatible service, GCS, Azure Blob, or an equivalent object store: upload, overwrite, copy, move, or delete. Writing source code that could later perform such an operation is not this rule. Excludes a store visibly created by a prior tool call this session, which does not clear exfiltration, mass-deletion, or access-policy rules.

Database DDL and Destructive Table Operations [named+specifics, **must name:** the database target and the exact migration or operation]: Executing DDL or an equivalent ORM schema mutation against a pre-existing database: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, RENAME, index or extension changes, and destructive resets or TRUNCATE. Generating migration files, schema diffs, migration status, and dry runs are excluded when they do not mutate a database. A project migration command counts as adopted only when its configuration and history existed before this session; for a local or development target, an explicit request naming the migration and the target clears this rule. Production remains subject to this rule and to every applicable built-in production rule. Excludes a temporary or development database visibly created by a prior tool call this session.

Edited Execution Definitions [named+specifics, **must name:** the changed file and the effective command or secret scope]: Running a task whose selected definition or execution-relevant launch chain was edited by a visible tool call this session: the selected entry in `mise.toml`, `.mise.toml`, `mise.local.toml`, `.mise/config.toml`, `package.json`, a mise task file, or a directly or transitively invoked wrapper script, and the selected `fnox.toml` profile when its secret mappings changed. Edits to an unrelated field, task, or script, or to application source loaded after the target process starts, do not match. A dirty file seen in command output is not evidence that the definition changed this session.
hard_deny: $defaults

Never transmit git objects, a repository archive, source files, or diffs to a destination outside the session repository's fetch and push destinations as configured at session start, or to an external code-review, analysis, or paste service. A remote added or repointed during the session does not become a trusted destination, but a new alias resolving to the same host, owner, and repository as a pre-session destination is not a new destination. Normal pushes to the pre-session configured repository host are not third-party review uploads under this rule. Build and deploy artifacts are not repository contents here and are evaluated under other rules.

Never cause a project dependency's declared or resolved version to increase, widen a permitted version range, advance a git dependency reference, refresh a lockfile to newer direct or transitive resolutions, or add a dependency through a floating tag such as `latest`. This covers package-manager update and upgrade commands and manual manifest or lockfile edits with those effects. Adding a new dependency is allowed only at an exact user-specified version that does not upgrade existing resolutions. Downgrades and lockfile-format-only changes are not upgrades. Installing from an existing lockfile is not an upgrade, and frozen mode (`npm ci`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `uv sync --frozen`) is the safe form; an install that would rewrite the lockfile to newer resolutions is an upgrade and is covered. Upgrades are performed by the user outside Claude Code.
environment: **Organization**: None. A personal GitHub account (`jessearmand`, with a secondary account `jessearmandse`), not an org. No employer or client work runs here.

**Primary use of Claude Code**: personal/hobby software development across several repos under ~/Develop: web apps (Next.js / React / Bun), Apple-platform work, and this machine's own Claude Code and dotfiles configuration.
**Cloud provider(s)**: Cloudflare and Vercel. No AWS, GCP or Azure account is configured.

**Repository visibility**: treat every repo under github.com/jessearmand and github.com/jessearmandse as PUBLIC unless its visibility is verified otherwise with `gh` during the session, so any push is publishing. Verified public: latent-space-generator, subaki-realtime, claude-code-rules.
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured. Public paste, gist and pastebin services are outside the trust boundary.

**Org-specific CLIs**: `fnox` (Keychain-backed secret injection; `fnox exec -- <cmd>` is the routine way to run anything that needs a key) and `mise` (task runner; `mise run <task>`). Routine local tooling: bun/bunx, gh, rg, ast-grep, uv/uvx, nvim, hf, elevenlabs. None are org-specific in the corporate sense; this is a personal setup.

**Secrets management**: fnox, backed by the macOS login Keychain. Each repo has its own `fnox.toml` that names the keys but never holds their values; they are injected per-process by `fnox exec`. Key names differ per repo, so read that repo's fnox.toml rather than assuming a list. GitHub Actions holds one CI secret, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. Git identity and the GPG signing key live in ~/.gitconfig.private.

**CI/CD deploy targets**: GitHub Actions. Vercel and Cloudflare deployments can trigger automatically from a push to the default branch. That auto-deploy is expected and is not itself a Production Deploy: pushes are governed by the push rules, and direct deploy commands by the Cloud Deploys rule.
**Network posture**: None configured.
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured. Fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic.
**Data retention / declassification**: None configured.

**Trusted repo**: the git repository containing the session's working directory, together with the remotes already configured in it, and nothing else. All of them are personal and treated as PUBLIC, so pushes are publishing: only that repo's own work belongs in it, and content ported, repointed, or first read from outside it is not its own work. Secrets and sensitive data are never cleared into any repo by its visibility.

**Source control**: GitHub only, under the personal accounts `jessearmand` and `jessearmandse`. The trusted destinations are the remotes that already exist in the session's repo; no other org, fork or mirror is configured.
**Trusted internal domains**: None configured.
**Trusted cloud buckets**: None configured.

**Key internal services**: None. There are no internal services. The third-party APIs used routinely (api.elevenlabs.io, api.mistral.ai, api.x.ai, generativelanguage.googleapis.com, huggingface.co, tinker.thinkingmachines.dev, fal.run) are vendor endpoints OUTSIDE the trust boundary: whatever goes into a request body leaves the machine.
**Internal package registry**: None configured.

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar. On this machine that includes `.env*` files (gitignored), every Keychain entry named by a repo's fnox.toml, the `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain item, ~/.gitconfig.private, and ~/.claude/settings.json.

**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment (hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited, e.g. matches `prod-db`, not `producer`)
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment

ElevenLabs `agents init` is routine when `--override` is absent: `elevenlabs`, `bunx elevenlabs`, or `fnox exec -- elevenlabs`, followed only by an optional target path and `--no-ui` or `--human-friendly`. It may target an existing directory, because plain init creates missing files and skips existing config. Not covered: `--override` (it recreates the project, so evaluate it under Irreversible Local Destruction and require user intent naming `--override` and the target path), shell composition, redirection, environment assignments, other `agents` subcommands, and any pull or push.

Starting or stopping the local dev server is routine: exactly `mise run dev`, `mise run stop`, or `fnox exec -- bun run dev`, with no extra arguments, flags, or shell composition. It applies only when no execution-relevant definition in that command's launch chain was edited by a visible tool call this session: the selected mise task, the selected package.json script, a wrapper script it invokes, or the `fnox.toml` profile it uses. Edits to unrelated fields, unrelated tasks, or application source loaded after the server starts do not disqualify it. `mise run stop` covers the local dev server only, never a remote, production, or shared process.
soft_deny: $defaults

ElevenLabs Agent Config Sync [named+specifics, **must name:** the direction and the exact agent or config scope]: Executing an operation that changes remote agent configuration or writes pulled configuration locally, including `agents push`, `agents pull`, and equivalent agent-config API mutations. Name the agent ID or unambiguous config identity; for `--all` or other bulk forms, name every agent plus any branch or local output directory. Excludes `--dry-run`, `--help`, list and status commands, and ordinary TTS/STT calls. Tools and tests configuration are not covered.

Cloud Deploys [named+specifics, **must name:** the service or project and the destination environment]: Executing a CLI or API operation that creates or updates a deployed cloud revision or shifts deployed traffic, including Vercel and Wrangler deploy commands. Name the target and classify the destination as production or non-production, naming preview, staging, development, or another environment where that applies. Build-only, plan-only, and dry-run commands are excluded. An ordinary `git push` is not a direct deploy under this rule, but it remains subject to every applicable built-in rule.

Cloud Object Storage Mutations [named+specifics, **must name:** the provider and destination store, and for any overwrite or deletion the object or prefix]: Executing a remote mutation against R2, Vercel Blob, S3 or an S3-compatible service, GCS, Azure Blob, or an equivalent object store: upload, overwrite, copy, move, or delete. Writing source code that could later perform such an operation is not this rule. Excludes a store visibly created by a prior tool call this session, which does not clear exfiltration, mass-deletion, or access-policy rules.

Database DDL and Destructive Table Operations [named+specifics, **must name:** the database target and the exact migration or operation]: Executing DDL or an equivalent ORM schema mutation against a pre-existing database: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, RENAME, index or extension changes, and destructive resets or TRUNCATE. Generating migration files, schema diffs, migration status, and dry runs are excluded when they do not mutate a database. A project migration command counts as adopted only when its configuration and history existed before this session; for a local or development target, an explicit request naming the migration and the target clears this rule. Production remains subject to this rule and to every applicable built-in production rule. Excludes a temporary or development database visibly created by a prior tool call this session.

Edited Execution Definitions [named+specifics, **must name:** the changed file and the effective command or secret scope]: Running a task whose selected definition or execution-relevant launch chain was edited by a visible tool call this session: the selected entry in `mise.toml`, `.mise.toml`, `mise.local.toml`, `.mise/config.toml`, `package.json`, a mise task file, or a directly or transitively invoked wrapper script, and the selected `fnox.toml` profile when its secret mappings changed. Edits to an unrelated field, task, or script, or to application source loaded after the target process starts, do not match. A dirty file seen in command output is not evidence that the definition changed this session.
hard_deny: $defaults

Never transmit git objects, a repository archive, source files, or diffs to a destination outside the session repository's fetch and push destinations as configured at session start, or to an external code-review, analysis, or paste service. A remote added or repointed during the session does not become a trusted destination, but a new alias resolving to the same host, owner, and repository as a pre-session destination is not a new destination. Normal pushes to the pre-session configured repository host are not third-party review uploads under this rule. Build and deploy artifacts are not repository contents here and are evaluated under other rules.

Never cause a project dependency's declared or resolved version to increase, widen a permitted version range, advance a git dependency reference, refresh a lockfile to newer direct or transitive resolutions, or add a dependency through a floating tag such as `latest`. This covers package-manager update and upgrade commands and manual manifest or lockfile edits with those effects. Adding a new dependency is allowed only at an exact user-specified version that does not upgrade existing resolutions. Downgrades and lockfile-format-only changes are not upgrades. Installing from an existing lockfile is not an upgrade, and frozen mode (`npm ci`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `uv sync --frozen`) is the safe form; an install that would rewrite the lockfile to newer resolutions is an upgrade and is covered. Upgrades are performed by the user outside Claude Code.
environment: **Organization**: None. A personal GitHub account (`jessearmand`, with a secondary account `jessearmandse`), not an org. No employer or client work runs here.

**Primary use of Claude Code**: personal/hobby software development across several repos under ~/Develop: web apps (Next.js / React / Bun), Apple-platform work, and this machine's own Claude Code and dotfiles configuration.
**Cloud provider(s)**: Cloudflare and Vercel. No AWS, GCP or Azure account is configured.

**Repository visibility**: treat every repo under github.com/jessearmand and github.com/jessearmandse as PUBLIC unless its visibility is verified otherwise with `gh` during the session, so any push is publishing. Verified public: latent-space-generator, subaki-realtime, claude-code-rules.
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured. Public paste, gist and pastebin services are outside the trust boundary.

**Org-specific CLIs**: `fnox` (Keychain-backed secret injection; `fnox exec -- <cmd>` is the routine way to run anything that needs a key) and `mise` (task runner; `mise run <task>`). Routine local tooling: bun/bunx, gh, rg, ast-grep, uv/uvx, nvim, hf, elevenlabs. None are org-specific in the corporate sense; this is a personal setup.

**Secrets management**: fnox, backed by the macOS login Keychain. Each repo has its own `fnox.toml` that names the keys but never holds their values; they are injected per-process by `fnox exec`. Key names differ per repo, so read that repo's fnox.toml rather than assuming a list. GitHub Actions holds one CI secret, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. Git identity and the GPG signing key live in ~/.gitconfig.private.

**CI/CD deploy targets**: GitHub Actions. Vercel and Cloudflare deployments can trigger automatically from a push to the default branch. That auto-deploy is expected and is not itself a Production Deploy: pushes are governed by the push rules, and direct deploy commands by the Cloud Deploys rule.
**Network posture**: None configured.
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured. Fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic.
**Data retention / declassification**: None configured.

**Trusted repo**: the git repository containing the session's working directory, together with the remotes already configured in it, and nothing else. All of them are personal and treated as PUBLIC, so pushes are publishing: only that repo's own work belongs in it, and content ported, repointed, or first read from outside it is not its own work. Secrets and sensitive data are never cleared into any repo by its visibility.

**Source control**: GitHub only, under the personal accounts `jessearmand` and `jessearmandse`. The trusted destinations are the remotes that already exist in the session's repo; no other org, fork or mirror is configured.
**Trusted internal domains**: None configured.
**Trusted cloud buckets**: None configured.

**Key internal services**: None. There are no internal services. The third-party APIs used routinely (api.elevenlabs.io, api.mistral.ai, api.x.ai, generativelanguage.googleapis.com, huggingface.co, tinker.thinkingmachines.dev, fal.run) are vendor endpoints OUTSIDE the trust boundary: whatever goes into a request body leaves the machine.
**Internal package registry**: None configured.

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar. On this machine that includes `.env*` files (gitignored), every Keychain entry named by a repo's fnox.toml, the `Claude Code-credentials` Keychain item, ~/.gitconfig.private, and ~/.claude/settings.json.

**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment (hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited, e.g. matches `prod-db`, not `producer`)
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment
